Arrows Rules

Send every arrow out of the field.

The rules

Moving
Tap an arrow. It slides out of the field in the direction its head points - but only if every square from its head to the edge is free. An arrow made of several squares follows its head; its own body must not lie in the way either.
Blocked
If another arrow is in the way, the tapped arrow stays where it is, and the arrow in the way gets a dotted frame. There is no penalty: take that arrow out first.
Gliding arrows (Hard and Master)
On Hard a blocked arrow does not stay put: it glides forward, body following head, up to the next arrow and stops there. That can block other arrows for good - think before you tap. Undo takes a move back, and Hint looks for a way out from where you are now. The arrows there have up to two corners and lie on 11 × 11 squares.
Master
As Hard, but with three hearts: every tap that does not take an arrow out of the field costs one. There is no hint and no frame for the arrow in the way. With no hearts left you can try the same puzzle again.
Goal
Clear the whole field. Every puzzle is made so that it can be solved, and taking an arrow out never blocks another one, so you cannot get stuck. The fewest moves are the number of arrows; Undo counts as a move too.
Levels
Easy: 5 × 5 squares with short arrows. Medium: 7 × 7 with arrows of two to four squares. Hard: 11 × 11 with gliding arrows of up to seven squares and two corners. Master: as Hard, with three hearts.
Hint
Hint marks an arrow that can leave now.

Example

The long arrow points right, but the short arrow stands in its way. The short arrow can leave upwards; after that the way is free for the long arrow.
